title: JSCAD text: outline / flat / round in one example
description: vectorText() gives polylines; the three builders turn them into a stroked outline, a flat extrude and a rounded sweep. Parameter declarations are declared in code, which is why this file is a good schema template.

parameters.name: height
parameters.description: extrusion height for the flat variant

constraints.why: stroke wider than ~40% of the cap height closes the counters (the holes in a/o/e) and the glyph stops reading

nomination.reason: stroke-based text (sketch font) is far more robust than TrueType outline extrusion at small sizes — Atta's text family should offer both

title: text() — the full parameter set of a 2D glyph run
description: text() produces a 2D geometric object from a font. size is the cap height in western scripts (default 10) and sets the em size to 100/72 of it; font is a logical fontconfig name (default 'Liberation Sans'); direction, language and script select flow and shaping; spacing multiplies the advance; $fn/$fs/$fa subdivide the glyph curves.

parameters.name: font
parameters.description: logical font name (fontconfig), optionally with a style

parameters.name: spacing
parameters.description: advance multiplier; 1 = the font's normal spacing

constraints.why: size is a cap-height, the em square is 100/72 of it — mixing the two is why text comes out ~39% larger than expected
glyph stems thinner than a nozzle width print as gaps, so small text must be engraved rather than embossed

notes: Paraphrase of the Wikibooks OpenSCAD manual Text page parameter list. Defaults quoted above are the documented defaults.

title: valign semantics: baseline is the only alignment that chains across runs
description: The manual distinguishes the four valign modes by *what* is pinned to the Y coordinate: top pins the tallest character, center pins the bounding-box centre (so descenders and tall letters move it), bottom pins the lowest descender, and baseline pins the font baseline. Baseline is the default and the only mode that aligns separate text runs as if on lined paper.

parameters.name: line_pitch
parameters.description: vertical distance between successive text runs; must exceed the em size or ascenders collide

constraints.why: manual: baseline is 'the only option that makes different pieces of text align vertically', because the other modes depend on the actual glyph extents of each run
runs closer than one em overlap ascenders and descenders

title: text() + linear_extrude as the canonical engraved-plate workflow
description: The manual's own example is `linear_extrude(15){ text("OpenSCAD", 50); }` — the text is created as a 2D region, then extruded to a plate-height solid. The engrave variant is the same stack with a difference(): extrude the text to the engraving depth and subtract it from the plate. Both signs of the same op are one parameter (depth, and a sign that picks emboss vs engrave).

parameters.name: size
parameters.description: text cap height passed to text()

parameters.name: depth
parameters.description: extrusion height — plate relief for emboss, cut depth for engrave

parameters.name: mode
parameters.description: sign of the boolean: engrave = plate minus text, emboss = plate plus text

parameters.name: plate_margin
parameters.description: border width around the text bounding box

constraints.why: engraving deeper than the plate removes it entirely; the manual's own example extrudes 15, so the plate must exceed that
shallow engraving below a nozzle width fills in on the first layer

nomination.reason: engrave and emboss are the same op with a sign; one family with a `mode` enum covers both and matches how a human asks for it

notes: Paraphrase; the manual's example is cited by shape (text + linear_extrude), not reproduced. Tier B (CC-BY-SA) so no code field.
